validity.recommendation: no action on identity -- P5832 is TEAM 2012 / FERC docket CP11-67; carry the capacity caveat in ResearcherNotes
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE AND IDENTITY: settled. P5832 is the Texas Eastern Appalachia to Market (TEAM) 2012 Expansion Project, FERC docket CP11-67-000/-001 (pre-filing PF10-21-000), built by Texas Eastern Transmission, LP and in service 2012-11-01. Independent of GEM entirely: four Federal Register notices in the docket (NOI 2010-08-26, Notice of Application 2011-02-11, Notice of Amendment 2011-06-30, EA availability 2011-09-02), FERC's in-service compliance filing entry (2012-09-12), a Pennsylvania DEP Chapter 105 permit notice naming the project (41 Pa.B. 3212, 2011-06-25), Spectra Energy's SEC filings (FY2011 10-K, Q3-2012 8-K), and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- NGA s.7 interstate natural gas TRANSMISSION loops plus compression, not gathering or distribution. DUPLICATE: no duplicate inside this batch's roster. The five other TETCO segment rows are distinct projects with distinct dockets -- P0235 OPEN (CP14-68, 76 mi, 550 MMcf/d), P0260 TEAM 2014 (CP13-84, 33.5 mi, 600 MMcf/d, $500M), P0261 TEAL (CP16-23, 950 MMcf/d), P2562 Middlesex Extension (CP20-30), P5835 Appalachia to Market (CP20-436, 0.8 mi, 30-inch, 18 MMcf/d, 2021) -- and none carries TEAM 2012's 17.3 mi / 36 in / 200 MMcf/d / $197M / 2012 signature. SPEC: every recorded value is corroborated by two or more independent origins (see fills). CAVEAT 1 -- capacity: FERC certificated 'approximately 190,000 dekatherms per day', while Spectra and EIA both publish 200 MMcf/d; Spectra's own figure moved 150 -> 190 -> 200 MMcf/d across its FY2009/FY2010/FY2011 10-Ks. The recorded 200 is the as-built operator/EIA figure and stands, but 190,000 Dth/d is the contracted firm increment. CAVEAT 2 -- length: the sheet's 17.3 mi is NEW LOOP mileage only; the project also abandoned ~11.3 mi of 24-inch pipe, correctly excluded. CAVEAT 3 -- this is an expansion, so the 200 MMcf/d is INCREMENTAL and must never be read as a Texas Eastern system figure. Harvested citation pool: P5832 carries 23 citations, every one of them from the shared Texas Eastern system gem.wiki page rather than from a TEAM 2012 document; I opened or resolved the ones that could bear on this row (the two Federal Register links -- 2011-22517, which IS this project's EA notice, and 2012-25206, which is a different docket's NOI and belongs to the TEAM/TEAL family; the Enbridge assets factsheet; the Hart Energy TEAM 2014 piece; the P&GJ OPEN piece) and found none that states a TEAM 2012 value; eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php in the pool is a navigation page and is never citable. The generic pool is why every unit here is sourced from the regulator, the operator's SEC filings, PA DEP and EIA instead.

validity.recommendation: change StartState/Province from West Virginia to Pennsylvania (both termini are Pennsylvania)
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records this row as West Virginia -> Pennsylvania. Every TEAM 2012 facility is in PENNSYLVANIA and no source places any part of the project in West Virginia. FERC's EA availability notice: 17.3 miles of 36-inch pipe 'in Greene, Fayette, Franklin, Adams and Fulton Counties, Pennsylvania', abandonment 'in Franklin and Adams Counties, Pennsylvania', compression added 'at its Bedford Compressor Station located in Bedford County, Pennsylvania'. The pre-filing NOI lists the same states and gives the four loops by county -- Holbrook West (Greene), Holbrook East (Fayette), Chambersburg (Franklin), Heidlersburg (Adams) -- all Pennsylvania. PA DEP's Chapter 105 notice for E28-369 confirms the Franklin County crossing work. The only West Virginia signal is EIA's coarse state coding 'WV,PA' (beg WV, end PA) on Historical Projects row 731, which describes the Appalachian supply direction rather than a facility; FERC's own description of the capacity path starts from 'supply points in Clarington, Ohio and the Appalachian area', i.e. Ohio, not West Virginia. The Greene County loop does sit on the West Virginia line, which is the likely origin of the coding. Sourced replacement staged on Location [ref]: Greene County, Pennsylvania -> Adams County, Pennsylvania, United States.

validity.recommendation: route candidate for §8 -- the merged geometry is the TETCO mainline corridor, not the 17.3 mi of TEAM 2012 loops; regrade RouteAccuracy to low pending a facility-level trace
validity.researcher_notes: ROUTE JUDGED FIRST, per the route-vs-sheet protocol. ../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P5832.geojson holds 7 LineString features, 512 points, every feature named simply 'Texas Eastern Transmission' with operator Spectra Energy / Enbridge and a `path` property pointing at the system file tx-east-v1.geojson -- i.e. generic OSM mainline ways, with nothing in the properties naming TEAM 2012. In plain words: the geometry's westernmost point is at the southwestern corner of Pennsylvania on the West Virginia line (about 39.88 N, 80.52 W, Greene County) and its easternmost is in south-central Pennsylvania (about 39.98 N, 76.99 W, Adams/York County area); read in feature order rather than flow order it forms TWO contiguous chains, one from 80.52 W to 79.38 W and one from 78.26 W to 76.99 W. Per-feature great-circle lengths are 6.0, 24.99, 11.97, 25.39, 28.44, 11.85 and 98.83 km, TOTAL 207.5 km = 128.9 miles. The project is 17.3 miles. CORRIDOR RIGHT, EXTENT WRONG: the two chains do fall across the right counties (Greene/Fayette in the southwest; Fulton/Franklin/Adams in the south-central band), which is exactly what the protocol warns about -- an expansion is loops and compressor stations scattered along a mainline, and a route that traces the mainline between the first and last facility overstates the project, here by about 7.5x. The sheet nonetheless reads RouteType = 'Mapped route (at any accuracy)' with RouteAccuracy = 'high'; 'high' is not defensible for a trace that is 7.5 times the certificated length and carries no TEAM 2012 identity in its properties. No coordinates are proposed. A corrected trace would digitize the four certificated loops only -- Holbrook West (1.8 mi, Greene), Holbrook East (4.7 mi as filed, cut ~1.47 mi by the June 2011 amendment, Fayette), Chambersburg (7.3 mi, Franklin) and Heidlersburg (4.0 mi, Adams) -- from the CP11-67 EA alignment sheets. RouteType stays 'Mapped route (at any accuracy)' (a merged geojson exists); only RouteAccuracy moves, so the three-way sync is preserved. The state cells are handled separately and on documents, not on this geometry. TIER: both refs are Federal Register notices (one publisher), and the 207.5 km extent is our own measurement of the repo geojson rather than a published figure -- single-origin, so medium, not high.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' confirmed, with evidence 13 years newer than the sheet's LastUpdated 2024-05-29. TEAM 2012 went into service 2012-11-01 (FERC in-service compliance filing effective 11/1/2012; Spectra Energy earnings release of 2012-11-01: 'the Philadelphia Lateral and TEAM 2012 projects are now in service and generating revenues'). MOST RECENT INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE, 2025-06-02: FERC's Notice of Application in docket CP25-491 (Appalachia to Market III, filed 2025-05-15) proposes to modify the Bedford Compressor Station 'by uprating the existing electric motor driven (EMD) compressor unit 13E from 26,000 horsepower (hp) to 35,500 hp ... and changing impellers on the existing EMD compressor units 11E and 12E'. Those are TEAM 2012's own units -- the project installed one new 26,000 hp EMD unit and uprated two 11,000 hp EMD units to 14,300 hp -- so the TEAM 2012 compression is demonstrably in service and being built upon in 2025, and Texas Eastern Transmission, LP is still the operator. EIA's August 2026 release still carries the project as Completed with in-service 2012. No evidence of idling, abandonment, conversion or sale of this scope; the owner changed from Spectra to Enbridge in 2017-18, which is an ownership fact, not a status change, and the sheet already records Enbridge. Not stale, not unclear: dated 2025 regulatory evidence exists.

cross_row_leads.facts: BEARING ON P2008's CONTESTED IDENTITY (staging dir deepsweep-remainder; NOT edited here). P5832 is definitively TEAM 2012 / FERC CP11-67: 17.3 mi of 36-inch loop in Greene, Fayette, Franklin, Adams and Fulton Counties PA plus 20,720 hp at the Bedford Compressor Station, amended cost $196,998,000, capacity increment ~190,000 Dth/d (operator/EIA 200 MMcf/d), in service 2012-11-01. P2008 records 53.10 km (33.0 mi) and $500M -- those are TEAM 2014's numbers exactly (FERC CP13-84; EIA Historical Projects row 785: 33.5 mi, 36 in, 600 MMcf/d, $500M, in-service 2014), and they match NOTHING about TEAM 2012. So P2008 is NOT this row's project: TEAM 2012 is fully accounted for by P5832, and normalizing P2008 onto TEAM 2012 would create a duplicate of P5832. P2008's staged Start of 2012-11, which came from the TEAM 2012 lineage, is internally inconsistent with its own recorded length and cost. The SegmentName-consistent alternative reading (TEMAX / TIME III, FERC CP09-68, 38.6 mi, 30/36 in, $472M, completed 2011-08-26, PA) matches neither P5832 nor TEAM 2014 exactly and remains the candidate to adjudicate. Recommendation for the orchestrator: whatever P2008 resolves to, it must not be TEAM 2012.
